title: A Weekend Trip to the Zoo
passage:
On Friday evening, Amy called her friend Ben on the phone. "Hi Ben, are you free this weekend? I'm going to visit the zoo with my cousin. Do you want to join us?" she asked.

Ben was excited. "Sure! I love animals, especially the ones that live in the rainforest. What time will we meet?"

"We will meet at the bus stop at nine o'clock," Amy said. "The bus that goes to the zoo leaves every thirty minutes, so we shouldn't be late."

Ben checked the weather forecast on his phone. "It says it might rain in the afternoon. Should we bring umbrellas?"

"That's a good idea," Amy replied. "I'll pack some snacks too, in case we get hungry. My cousin, who works at an animal hospital, knows a lot about wild animals. She can tell us interesting facts."

On Saturday morning, the three friends met at the bus stop. The weather was sunny, but dark clouds were forming in the sky. "I think it's going to rain later," Ben said, looking up. They walked into the zoo and saw elephants, tigers, and monkeys that were playing near a small pond.

Suddenly, it started to rain. They quickly opened their umbrellas and laughed. "I'm glad we brought these!" Amy said. After the rain stopped, they visited the reptile house, which had colorful snakes and lizards.

By the end of the day, everyone agreed that it was one of the best weekends they had ever had. "Let's plan another trip next month," Ben suggested, and they all happily agreed.

vocab.example: The weather forecast says it will rain tomorrow.
Don't forget your umbrella; it might rain.
Many wild animals live in the rainforest.
The children were excited to see the elephants.
The ducks are swimming in the pond.
I packed some snacks for the trip.
Do you want to join us for lunch?
Ben suggested visiting the zoo again.
Everyone agreed that it was a fun day.
Wild animals should not be kept as pets.
Dark clouds appeared in the sky.

grammar: 未來式 will vs. be going to：be going to 表示事先計畫好的打算或有跡象顯示即將發生的事（I'm going to visit the zoo、dark clouds...it's going to rain）；will 表示當下決定或單純未來的預測與承諾（We will meet at the bus stop、I'll pack some snacks）。

關係代名詞 who / which / that：who 代替「人」作主詞（my cousin, who works at an animal hospital）；which 代替「物」作主詞，常用於補充說明的子句（the reptile house, which had colorful snakes）；that 可代替人或物，常用於限定子句（the bus that goes to the zoo、monkeys that were playing）。

reading.q: Why did Amy call Ben on Friday evening?
opts: To invite him to the zoo
reading.ex: 文中提到 Amy 打電話問 Ben「I'm going to visit the zoo with my cousin. Do you want to join us?」，是邀請他一起去動物園。

reading.q: What time will Amy and Ben meet at the bus stop?
reading.ex: 文中提到「We will meet at the bus stop at nine o'clock」。

reading.q: Why did Amy decide to bring snacks?
opts: Because the zoo has no food
reading.ex: 文中提到「I'll pack some snacks too, in case we get hungry.」。

reading.q: What did the friends do when it started to rain?
opts: Ran back to the bus stop
reading.ex: 文中提到「They quickly opened their umbrellas and laughed.」。

reading.q: What did they see in the reptile house?
reading.ex: 文中提到「the reptile house, which had colorful snakes and lizards」。

grammar.q: Choose the correct sentence for a plan already decided: "I ______ visit the zoo this weekend."
grammar.ex: be going to 用於表達事先已經計畫好的打算，故用 am going to。

grammar.q: Fill in the relative pronoun: "My cousin, ______ works at an animal hospital, knows a lot about animals."
grammar.ex: 先行詞 my cousin 是「人」，作子句主詞，故用 who。

grammar.q: "The bus ______ goes to the zoo leaves every thirty minutes." (選出正確的關係代名詞)
grammar.ex: 先行詞 the bus 是「物」，作子句主詞，故用 which（或 that）。

grammar.q: Which sentence correctly uses "will" for a decision made at the moment of speaking?
opts: I'm going to pack some snacks tomorrow.
grammar.ex: will 常用於說話當下臨時決定要做的事，故 I'll pack some snacks too. 正確。

grammar.q: "Dark clouds were forming in the sky. I think it ______ rain later." (根據跡象做預測)
grammar.ex: 根據眼前跡象（烏雲）做出的預測要用 be going to，故為 is going to。

vocab.q: "Snakes and lizards are ______." (選出意思為「爬蟲類」的單字)
"The weather ______ says it will rain tomorrow." (選出意思為「預報」的單字)
